verses.1: And they traveled from Eilam. All the tribes of the Israelites came to the Mediterranean Sea, which lies between Eilam and Sinai. This happened on the fifteenth day of the second month after they left Egypt.
verses.2: And all the tribes of the children of Israel mourned over Moses and Aaron in the valley.
verses.3: And the children of Israel said to them, “Who will give us death in the land of Egypt? We are dying from hunger while eating unleavened bread. It’s like being sent out into the desert just to die from starvation.”
verses.4: And the LORD said to Moses, “I will bring you bread from heaven.” So the people went out and gathered some of it in order to eat. They did this so that they could follow My laws. Otherwise, they would not be able to go along with them.
verses.5: And on the sixth day, they would prepare what they were to bring. It would be a mixture of everything that was collected each day.
verses.6: And Moses and Aaron said to all the children of Israel, “In the evening, know that Jehovah has brought you out of the land of Egypt.”
verses.7: And in the morning, when they saw the glory of Jehovah, they heard your praises about Jehovah. Then they became quiet, because you had praised Jehovah upon us.
verses.8: And Moses said to you, “In the evening, eat bread and meat; in the morning, listen to God’s words. For you are going to pray to Him about your troubles. What else can we do but pray to God for help?”
verses.9: And Moses said to Aaron, “Tell all the tribes of Israel to come forward before Jehovah, for they have heard your prayers.”
verses.10: And when Aaron spoke to all the tribes of Israel, they turned toward the sea. And there was a sight before them: the glory of the LORD appeared in the clouds.
verses.11: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.12: I heard the cries of the children of Israel as they were told, “In the evenings, you shall eat meat; in the mornings, you shall eat bread. And know that I, the LORD your God, am with you.”
verses.13: In the morning, the clouds covered the camp. In the evening, a layer of darkness covered the camp.
verses.14: And the clouds of rain covered the surface of the sea. It was like a thin layer of water covering the land.
verses.15: And the children of Israel saw this, and they said to each other, “Who is this man? We don’t know who he is.” Moses said to them, “This is the bread that Jehovah has given you to eat.”
verses.16: This is what the LORD commanded: that no one should eat from it, according to how much each person has eaten. Each person must bring back to the tent those items that they have eaten.
verses.17: And so did the children of Israel. They gathered together all the grain and the fruits.
verses.18: And they ate in the tent. Neither the hunger nor the desire for food prevented anyone from eating.
verses.19: And Moses said to them, “There is no one more powerful than me until tomorrow.”
verses.20: And they did not listen to Moses. So people rushed away from him until evening. Then Moses threw stones at them and became angry with them.
verses.21: And they gathered him in the morning, at dawn. One man ate him, and the heat of the sun made him sick.
verses.22: And on the sixth day, they baked new bread from two loaves. Then all the men of the congregation came and said to Moses:
verses.23: And he said to them, “This is what the LORD has commanded regarding Shabbat: that no one should work on it, nor should they do anything that would violate its sanctity. And all those things that are forbidden during Shabbat must be kept holy for you until tomorrow.”
verses.24: They left him there until morning, as Moses commanded. No one came to take him away; and no one tried to steal him away.
verses.25: And Moses said, “Eat it today, for this is the Sabbath day. Today, it belongs to the Lord. You will not find it in the field today.”
verses.26: For six days, it will be gathered together; but on the seventh day, Shabbat shall not be observed.
verses.27: And on the seventh day, the people went out to gather crops, but they did not find anything.
verses.28: And the LORD said to Moses, “Until now, you have not kept my commandments and my laws.”
verses.29: See, Jehovah has given you the Sabbath. Therefore, on the seventh day, He will give you bread to eat. On that day, no one shall leave his place. No one shall go anywhere else on that day.
verses.30: And the people sat down on the fifth day.
verses.31: And the house of Israel called out his name. His name was like a white seed; its taste was like that of mint.
verses.32: And Moses said, “This is what the LORD has commanded: You must keep these words in your hearts, so that you may fear the LORD. This is because I ate those foods with you at the desert, when I brought you out of Egypt.”
verses.33: And Moses said to Aaron, “Take one of the censers and fill it with the smoke of the incense. Then place it before Jehovah, so that it may serve as a reminder of your duties.”
verses.34: When Jehovah commanded Moses, Aaron was placed in charge of overseeing the altar.
verses.35: And the children of Israel ate the land for forty years, until they reached the land that was to be given to them as an inheritance. They ate the land until they reached the ends of the earth.
verses.36: And the verse is twelve words long.
